title: 1973 AHSME Problem 8

concepts.label: Power scaling of length, area, and volume

statement: If \(1\) pint of paint is needed to paint a statue \(6\) ft. high, then the number of pints it will take to paint (to the same thickness) \(540\) statues similar to the original but only \(1\) ft. high is

solutions.text:
A \(1\)-ft. statue has linear scale \(\frac{1}{6}\) relative to the original, so its surface area and paint requirement are \(\frac{1}{36}\) as large. The \(540\) small statues therefore require \[ 540\cdot\frac1{36}=15 \] pints.

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Paint required scales with surface area, not volume
Reducing every length by a factor of \(6\) reduces the paint per statue by the square of that factor
